open_points.subject: A17 configuration path traversal
open_points.text: The kernel reads the file's path from its one command-line argument ... the path is opened component by component without following a symbolic link at any of them
open_points.question: Must the configuration path be absolute, or are relative paths, `.` and `..` components accepted, and from which directory is a relative path resolved?
options: require an absolute path with no `.` or `..` components
accept relative paths resolved from the process working directory
accept both forms but normalize lexical components before opening
open every supplied component literally, including `.` and `..`
open_points.default_guess: Require an absolute path and reject `.` and `..` components.

open_points.subject: A17 component opens
open_points.question: Which access flags and type checks apply to intermediate path components, and therefore which directory permissions and non-directory components cause refusal?
options: open intermediate components with `O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW`
open them read-only with `O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW`
use another `openat`-style combination and require only that traversal succeeds
open_points.default_guess: Use `O_PATH|O_DIRECTORY|O_NOFOLLOW` for intermediate directories and open the final file separately with `O_NOFOLLOW`.

open_points.subject: A17 and A20 O_NOFOLLOW assumption
open_points.text: each component with Linux's `O_NOFOLLOW`, whose presence no code tests (A20 rule 3)
open_points.question: What must happen if the Python/runtime interface or the mounted filesystem does not support `O_NOFOLLOW`, despite the host identifying as Linux?
options: the release assumes support and may fail as an internal/startup error
configuration opening refuses start and credential opening yields `credential_unresolved`
the host is outside the supported Linux set, but that set must be defined
open_points.default_guess: Treat failure while opening configuration as a startup refusal and failure while opening a credential as `credential_unresolved`.

open_points.subject: A18 data-directory initialization
open_points.text: At start it takes an exclusive lock in the data directory ... The data directory holds one SQLite database
open_points.question: Must the data directory and its layout already exist, or may the kernel create the directory, database, value areas and spool areas; and what happens when only part of the layout exists?
options: the complete layout must pre-exist
the directory must exist but the kernel creates missing internal files and subdirectories
the kernel creates the directory and all missing layout
any partial layout is corruption and stops start
open_points.default_guess: Require the configured directory to exist and create missing kernel-owned database and subdirectories after validating it.

open_points.subject: A18 exclusive process lock
open_points.text: At start it takes an exclusive lock in the data directory; a second process on the same directory refuses to start.
open_points.question: What object and Linux locking primitive define the exclusive lock, how long is it held, and how are missing, stale, malformed or otherwise unopenable lock objects classified?
options: a fixed regular lock file with an advisory `flock` held for process lifetime
a fixed regular lock file with a POSIX record lock held for process lifetime
an atomically created owner file whose stale state is detected and removed
a lock on the data-directory descriptor
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed regular lock file and hold a nonblocking advisory `flock` for the process lifetime; any lock-object error other than contention refuses startup with a distinct reason.

open_points.subject: A18 private data directory
open_points.text: The directory and everything in it are private to the kernel's user; the kernel refuses to start otherwise.
open_points.question: What exact ownership and mode conditions mean `private`, which nested entries are checked, and must those conditions continue to be enforced after startup and on every newly created file?
options: every entry must be owned by the kernel user with no group or other permissions
only the data-directory root must have those ownership and mode properties
directories may have restricted group access but payload files may not
check recursively only at startup
check at startup and again whenever an entry is opened, while creating every entry with fixed private modes
open_points.default_guess: Require the root and every nested entry to be owned by the kernel user with no group or other permissions, check existing entries at startup and opened entries thereafter, and create new entries with owner-only modes.

open_points.subject: A18 allowed filesystem entry types
open_points.text: The data directory holds one SQLite database, a content-addressed area of value bytes and file fixtures named by digest, and the run spool ... Every file of the directory is opened without following symbolic links
open_points.question: Are hard links, FIFOs, sockets, devices and unexpected regular files or directories permitted anywhere in the data directory, and what must startup or a later store call do on finding them?
options: only the expected directories and regular files with link count one are permitted
all non-symbolic entry types are permitted if permissions are private
special files are refused but unexpected private regular files are retained
unexpected entries are deleted during startup cleanup
open_points.default_guess: Permit only the expected directories and regular files with link count one; refuse startup or the encountering store call for other entry types, while retaining unrecognized private regular files unless explicitly classified as cleanup artifacts.

open_points.subject: A18 symlink-safe traversal
open_points.text: Every file of the directory is opened without following symbolic links; a link found at start stops the start, and one found later makes that store call fail with nothing written.
open_points.question: Does the no-follow requirement apply component by component to directories as well as to the final file, and how must the implementation prevent a directory from being replaced by a symlink between the startup scan and a later open?
options: hold and traverse directory descriptors with `openat` and `O_NOFOLLOW` on every component
check the path with metadata before an ordinary final-component no-follow open
rescan the entire data directory before every store call
open_points.default_guess: Traverse from an already opened data-directory descriptor and open every component with no-follow semantics.

open_points.subject: A18 request serialization
open_points.text: Surface requests are handled one at a time in the order they arrive
open_points.question: What defines arrival order when two requests are received concurrently or become readable together, and is that order required to be reproducible or externally observable?
options: the listener assigns a monotonic sequence when a complete request is received
the listener assigns a sequence when request processing begins
the transport/runtime's scheduling order is accepted
concurrent arrival is refused or impossible by construction
open_points.default_guess: Assign a monotonic sequence when each complete request is accepted from the transport and process by that sequence.

open_points.subject: A18 store-call transaction boundaries
open_points.text: Every change is one call to the store module and one transaction inside it
open_points.question: Which groups of record and file changes constitute one `change` and therefore one atomic store call, especially for admission, activation, run advancement, cancellation, release and startup cleanup where the other rules describe multiple related writes?
options: each surface action is one store call and transaction
each logical step explicitly described by a rule is one store call, allowing a request to make several commits
each individual record mutation is one store call except where another rule explicitly requires a group
the later module design may choose transaction grouping
open_points.default_guess: Treat each explicitly described logical transition as one store call, grouping records only where a rule expressly says they are written together.

open_points.subject: A18 store record order
open_points.text: one writer ... no record ever has two orders
open_points.question: What event assigns a record's immutable store position, whether updates to mutable entities receive new positions, and how positions are ordered when one transaction creates several records?
options: a global sequence is assigned only when each record is first created, with a specified within-transaction insertion order
every mutation receives a new global event position while the entity retains its creation position
SQLite row identifiers or commit order implicitly define position
each record type has a separate order
open_points.default_guess: Assign every newly created record a value from one global increasing sequence, never change that position on updates, and prescribe the sequence of records created together.

open_points.subject: A18 file publication durability
open_points.text: written to a temporary file, flushed, checked against their digest and size, and then renamed into place; a completed file a record names is never overwritten
open_points.question: What does `flushed` require, where must the temporary file reside, when are the containing directory and SQLite transaction made durable, and what crash states are permitted between rename and database commit?
options: same-directory temporary file, file `fsync`, atomic rename, directory `fsync`, then database commit with durable SQLite settings
same-filesystem temporary file and ordinary buffered flush are sufficient
rename precedes the database transaction and orphan cleanup handles every crash point
database commit precedes rename and startup repairs missing files
open_points.default_guess: Create the temporary file in the target directory, `fsync` it, rename atomically, `fsync` the directory, then commit the referencing database transaction with durable SQLite settings; an intervening crash may leave only an unreferenced complete file.

open_points.subject: A18 SQLite failure and corruption handling
open_points.text: The data directory holds one SQLite database with every kernel record
open_points.question: What must startup do when the database is absent, malformed, corrupt, locked by an unrelated process, has an unsupported schema, or cannot provide the durability and transaction behavior the rules assume?
options: create only an absent database and refuse every other condition
refuse all conditions including absence
attempt automatic repair or migration
accept supported older schemas and migrate them
open_points.default_guess: Create an absent database for a valid new data directory, but refuse startup for corruption, unsupported schema, unexpected locks or unavailable required SQLite guarantees.

open_points.subject: A18 startup cleanup failures
open_points.text: On start, temporary files, value bytes no record names ... and the spool directories of runs that ended and do not keep their spool ... are removed; nothing else is. A spool directory that cannot be removed does not stop the start
open_points.question: Does failure to remove a temporary file or unreferenced value byte also allow startup to continue, as explicitly stated only for spool directories, or does it stop startup?
options: all cleanup failures are tolerated and retried at a later start
only spool-directory removal failures are tolerated; other cleanup failures stop startup
temporary-file failures are tolerated but unreferenced-value failures stop startup
open_points.default_guess: Apply the stated exception only to spool directories; failure to remove other required cleanup artifacts stops startup.

open_points.subject: A18 content-address collision handling
open_points.text: Equal bytes are stored once ... a completed file a record names is never overwritten
open_points.question: What happens when the target digest path already exists but its bytes, size or expected type do not match the bytes being published, whether because of corruption or a SHA-256 collision?
options: verify the existing file and fail without writing on any mismatch
trust the digest and reuse the existing file without rereading it
quarantine the existing file and replace it
stop the kernel because the store is corrupt
open_points.default_guess: Verify the existing file; on mismatch write no record, report store corruption and stop the kernel after the internal-error response.

open_points.subject: A20 Linux host boundary
open_points.text: A release runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named
open_points.question: What exactly qualifies a host as Linux, and how and when must the kernel refuse to run on a non-Linux or compatibility-layer host?
options: check the runtime platform identifier before any data-directory access
rely on packaging and make no runtime host check
accept Linux ABI compatibility layers even when the reported host is not Linux
require a native Linux kernel and verify it with a specified system call
open_points.default_guess: Check the runtime-reported operating system before opening installation or store data and refuse startup unless it reports Linux.

open_points.subject: A20 Linux compatibility baseline
open_points.text: A release runs on Linux and on no other host, no version named
open_points.question: Without a Linux version or capability baseline, which kernel, libc, CPU architecture and filesystem implementations are supported, and what happens when Linux lacks semantics required by namespaces, `O_NOFOLLOW`, resource limits, locking, SQLite or atomic durable rename?
options: every Linux version and environment is claimed to be supported
support is capability-based and startup probes every required capability
the release declares a kernel/libc/architecture/filesystem baseline despite naming no Linux version
only the bubblewrap probe is required and later unsupported operations fail in place
open_points.default_guess: Define support by required capabilities and refuse startup when a capability needed for safe operation is unavailable.
